summary.para:
A body is contained within a world and has 3 degrees-of-freedom, two for position and one for rotation. A body can have forces, torques and impulses applied to it. A body has three distinct types:
- Static: This type of body does not move under simulation and behaves as if it has infinite mass, essentially an immovable object. Static bodies never interact with other Static or Kinematic bodies. - Dynamic: This type of body is fully simulated and moves according to forces and torques applied to its linearangular velocities. It can interact with all other body types. It always has finite, non-zero mass. - Kinematic: This type of body moves under simulation and moves according to its linearangular velocities and never uses forces or torques. It only interacts with Dynamic body types. It behaves as if it has infinite mass.
A body is automatically destroyed when the world it is in is destroyed. A body cannot exist outside a world.
The angular damping of the body. This will reduce the angular velocity over time. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody._angularVelocity.
The angular velocity of the body, in degrees per second.
The awake state of the body.

Get/Set the Object that event callbacks for this body will be sent to. Care should be taken with any Object assigned as a callback target that isn't a Object as this assignment will not in itself keep the object alive and can be garbage collected. To avoid this, you should have at least a single reference to the object in your code. To remove the object assigned here, set the callback target to NULL.
This includes the following events:
- A Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsEvents.BodyUpdateEvent with call Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsCallbacks.IBodyUpdateCallback.

A threshold used to control when continuous collision detection is used when a body moves. The value is used to compare the body linear velocity movement against the extents of all the shapes added to the body scaled by this threshold. If the movement exceeds the extents scaled by the threshold then continuous collision detection is used to stop tunneling. Lower values reduce the distance the body must move before continuous collision detection is used and can have a considerable impact on performance! Higher values increase the distance the body must move before continuous collision detection is used. Too low a threshold will result in continuous collision detection being used more often therefore affecting performance so this should be limited to specific bodies only. The default threshold is 0.5 which equates to half the total shape extents. The threshold is clamped to a range of 0.0 to 1.0 with 0.0 meaning continuous collision detection will always be used.
Get/Set the degrees of freedom constraints (locks) for the body of Linear X, Linear Y and Rotation Z.

Controls contact recycling for this body. Enabled by default. Contact recycling reuses contact manifolds when bodies move only slightly, improving performance. Disabling it can avoid ghost collisions, at the cost of higher simulation time. Both bodies in a contact must have recycling enabled for that contact to be recycled. Existing contacts retain their prior setting; only contacts created after a change will be recycled. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBodyDefinition._contactRecyclingAllowed.

Get/Set a body definition by accessing all of its current properties. This is provided as convenience only and should not be used when performance is important as all the properties defined in the definition are accessed sequentially. You should try to only use the specific properties you need rather than using this feature.
The enabled state of the body. If false, the body and anything attached to it will not participate in the simulation.

Treat this body as high speed object that performs continuous collision detection against dynamic and kinematic bodies, but not other high speed bodies. Fast collision bodies should be used sparingly. They are not a solution for general dynamic-versus-dynamic continuous collision.
This allows this body to bypass rotational speed limits. This should only be used for circular objects, such as wheels, balls etc.

Scales the world gravity that is applied to this body. Setting the gravity scale to zero stops any gravity being applied. Likewise, a negative value inverts gravity. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._gravity.
Get if the body is owned. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody.SetOwner.
Checks if a body is valid.
Get the number of joints attached to this body. Use Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody.GetJoints to retrieve the joints.
The linear damping of the body. This will reduce the linear velocity over time. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody._linearVelocity.
The linear velocity of the body.

The center of mass position of the body in local space. This can be accessed as a union of Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody._mass, Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody._rotationalInertia and Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody._localCenterOfMass using Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody._massConfiguration.

The calculated mass of the body, usually in kilograms. This can be accessed as a union of Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody._mass, Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody._rotationalInertia and Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody._localCenterOfMass using Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody._massConfiguration.

The body mass configuration comprised of the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody._mass, Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody._rotationalInertia and Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody._localCenterOfMass. Normally this is computed automatically as each Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape is added, removed or changed on a body. This will automatically change if the body type changes, for instance, a Static or Kinematic body always have zero mass and rotational inertia. The individual properties of the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody._massConfiguration and be accessed using Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody._mass, Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody._rotationalInertia and Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody._localCenterOfMass. The Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody.MassConfiguration will be overwritten when setting this property or if Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody.ApplyMassFromShapes is called or when adding, removing or changing Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape with Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShapeDefinition._startMassUpdate enabled.
Get Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsUserData that can be used for any purpose, typically by the owner only.
Get the physics handle.
The position of the body in the world.
The rotation of the body.

The rotational inertia of the body, usually in kg*m^2. This can be accessed as a union of Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody._mass, Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody._rotationalInertia and Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody._localCenterOfMass using Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody._massConfiguration.
Get the number of shapes attached to this body. Use Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody.GetShapes to retrieve the shapes.
The sleeping ability of the body. If false, the body will never sleep and will be woken up. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody._awake.
The threshold below which the body will sleep, in meters/sec.
The total user force that has been applied to this body since the last simulation step. Setting this value overrides any force that was previously requested.
The total users torque that has been applied to this body since the last simulation step. Setting this value overrides any torque that was previously requested.
The full transform of the body composed of position and rotation.

GetSet the transform object associated with the body. This can be used as a write transform andor as a depth-hint for Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld drawing. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody._transformWriteMode.

Get/Set how the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody._transformObject should be written to after the simulation has completed. Transform write will only occur if it is enabled on the world using Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._transformWriteMode.
A body is one of these three body types, Dynamic, Kinematic or Static, each of which determines how the body behaves in the simulation.
Get/Set Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsUserData that can be used for any purpose. The physics system doesn't use this data, it is entirely for custom use.
Get the world the body is attached to.
Get the center of mass position of the body in world space. This changes as the body moves i.e. as the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody._transform is changed.
Controls whether this body is automatically drawn when the world is drawn.

summary.para: Typically a body will automatically calculate the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody.MassConfiguration using all the attached shapes. The Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody.MassConfiguration is automatically updated whenever a Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape is added, removed or modified. When adding many shapes to a body, you can choose to stop this automatic calculation, therefore improving performance, by disabling Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShapeDefinition._startMassUpdate for each shape being added to the body. This call will result in the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody.MassConfiguration being calculated using the currently added Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape so is typically called after many shapes are added if they have Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShapeDefinition._startMassUpdate disabled. Alternately, if you wish to assign your own Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody.MassConfiguration then disabling the automatic calculation also makes sense. In either case, you must call this method or set Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody._massConfiguration before any simulation step occurs otherwise the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody will exhibit unstable collision behaviour. The Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody.MassConfiguration will be overwritten when calling Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody.ApplyMassFromShapes, if Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody._massConfiguration is set or when adding, removing or changing Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape with Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShapeDefinition._startMassUpdate enabled.

When the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody.TransformWriteTween._transformWriteMode is Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody.TransformWriteMode.Interpolate, this defines the target pose to move to. When the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody.TransformWriteTween._transformWriteMode is Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody.TransformWriteMode.Extrapolate, this defines the source pose to move from.

When the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody.TransformWriteTween._transformWriteMode is Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody.TransformWriteMode.Current, this is set to the last Transform._position. but is not used. When the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody.TransformWriteTween._transformWriteMode is Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody.TransformWriteMode.Interpolate, this is set to the last Transform._position. When the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody.TransformWriteTween._transformWriteMode is Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody.TransformWriteMode.Extrapolate, this will be calculated from Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody.TransformWriteTween._physicsTransform. When the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody.TransformWriteTween._transformWriteMode is Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody.TransformWriteMode.Interpolate, this is set to the last Transform._rotation. When the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody.TransformWriteTween._transformWriteMode is Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody.TransformWriteMode.Extrapolate, this will be calculated from Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody.TransformWriteTween._physicsTransform. This is NOT set when the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._transformTweenMode is set to Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.TransformTweenMode.Parallel and will be zero.

summary.para: A Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody definition used to specify important initial properties.

Angular damping is used to reduce the angular velocity over time i.e. slow down rotating bodies. The damping parameter can be larger than 1.0f but the damping effect becomes sensitive to the time step when the damping parameter is large.
The initial angular velocity of the body, in degrees per second.
Is this body initially awake or sleeping?

A threshold used to control when continuous collision detection is used when a body moves. The value is used to compare the body linear velocity movement against the extents of all the shapes added to the body scaled by this threshold. If the movement exceeds the extents scaled by the threshold then continuous collision detection is used to stop tunneling. Lower values reduce the distance the body must move before continuous collision detection is used and can have a considerable impact on performance! Higher values increase the distance the body must move before continuous collision detection is used. Too low a threshold will result in continuous collision detection being used more often therefore affecting performance so this should be limited to specific bodies only. The default threshold is 0.5 which equates to half the total shape extents. The threshold is clamped to a range of 0.0 to 1.0 with 0.0 meaning continuous collision detection will always be used.
The degrees of freedom constraints (locks) for the body of Linear X, Linear Y and Rotation Z.

Controls contact recycling for this body. Enabled by default. Contact recycling reuses contact manifolds when bodies move only slightly, improving performance. Disabling it can avoid ghost collisions, at the cost of higher simulation time. Both bodies in a contact must have recycling enabled for that contact to be recycled.
See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody._contactRecyclingAllowed.
Get a default Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody definition.
Used to disable a body. A disabled body does not move or collide.

Treat this body as high speed object that performs continuous collision detection against dynamic and kinematic bodies, but not other high speed bodies. Fast collision bodies should be used sparingly. They are not a solution for general dynamic-versus-dynamic continuous collision.
This allows this body to bypass rotational speed limits. This should only be used for circular objects, such as wheels, balls etc.
Scale the gravity applied to this body, non-dimensional.

Linear damping is use to reduce the linear velocity i.e. slow down translating bodies. The damping parameter can be larger than 1 but the damping effect becomes sensitive to the time step when the damping parameter is large. Generally linear damping is undesirable because it makes objects move slowly as if they are floating.
The initial linear velocity of the body's origin, in meters/sec.

The initial position of the body, in world-space. Bodies should be created with the desired position as creating bodies at the origin and then moving them nearly doubles the cost of body creation, especially if the body is moved after shapes have been added.

The initial rotation of the body, in world-space. Bodies should be created with the desired rotation as creating bodies at the origin and then rotating them nearly doubles the cost of body creation, especially if the body is moved after shapes have been added.
Set this flag to false if this body should never fall asleep.
A speed threshold below which the body is allowed to sleep, in meters/sec.
The method used to Write the body pose to the Transform.

member.name: M:Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsCallbacks.IContactFilterCallback.OnContactFilter2D(Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsEvents/ContactFilterEvent)

summary.para:
Called when a pair of shapes are determined to be in contact. This is called to decide if a contact will be created for these shapes, allowing contact creation to be bypassed so a contact will not go to the solver. This is only called if the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld has Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._contactFilterCallbacks set to true. An event is only produced if one of the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape have Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape._contactFilterCallbacks set to true. This is called for both triggers and non-triggers but only with Dynamic bodies.
Extreme care must be taken with this callback!!
This callback occurs during the simulation step and can be called from any thread, therefore it must be thread-safe. During this time, the simulation state is undefined for the broadphase, events etc. For this reason, any attempt to perform a write operation will result in a deadlock as the world itself is write locked. Performing simple read operations on Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody, Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape or Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsJoint is safe, such as reading velocity or getting the geometry of a shape however, more complex operations involving the world such as performing a query can result in corruption or crashes. A recommendation is reading Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsUserData from any object which is a completely safe read operation therefore any required information should be encoded there if possible.

member.param: The event that occurred.

returns.para: Return false if you do not want a contact to be created during this simulation step. Returning true allows the contact to be created.

member.name: M:Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsCallbacks.IPreSolveCallback.OnPreSolve2D(Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsEvents/PreSolveEvent)

summary.para:
Called when a contact between a pair of shapes is updated. This allows a contact to be disabled before it goes to the solver. A typical use-case would be to implement a one-way behaviour based upon the provided contact. This is only called if the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld has Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._preSolveCallbacks set to true. An event is only produced if one of the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape have Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape._preSolveCallbacks set to true. This is only called for Awake Dynamic bodies. This is not called for triggers.
Extreme care must be taken with this callback!!
This callback occurs during the simulation step and can be called from any thread, therefore it must be thread-safe. During this time, the simulation state is undefined for the broadphase, events etc. For this reason, any attempt to perform a write operation will result in a deadlock as the world itself is write locked. Performing simple read operations on Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody, Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape or Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsJoint is safe, such as reading velocity or getting the geometry of a shape, however more complex operations involving the world such as performing a query can result in corruption or crashes. A recommendation is to use the provided contact details to make a decision in the callback. An additional recommendation is reading Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsUserData from any object which is a completely safe read operation therefore any required information should be encoded there if possible.

member.param: The event that occurred.

returns.para: Return false if you want to disable the contact this simulation step. Returning true allows the contact.

A dedicated shape that produces a chain of shapes connected together to produce a continuous surface. Chain shapes provide a smooth, continuous surface that will not produce "ghost" collisions. A Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsChain is automatically destroyed when the body it is in is destroyed. A Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsChain cannot exist unattached from a body.
This will produce shapes of type Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape.ShapeType.ChainSegment.
- Chains are one-sided. - A chain has no mass therefore should ideally be used on static bodies. - A chain can have a counter-clockwise winding order (normal points right of segment direction). - A chain is either a loop or open. - A chain must have at least 4 points. - The distance between any two points must be greater than Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._linearSlop. - A chain should not self intersect (this is not validated). - An open chain has no collision on the first and final edge. - You may overlap two open chains on their first three and/or last three points to get smooth collision.

Get the world AABB that bounds this chain. The bounds of the shape is inflated slightly due to speculative collision detection. The inflation is smaller on Static shape types however it is not zero due to time-of-impact collision detection. If an exact AABB is required then you can retrieve that via the shape geometry.
The body which the chain is attached to.
The bounciness of the chain. Usually this is within the range [0, 1]. Values higher than 1 will result in energy being added which can lead to an unstable simulation.
Defines the method used when mixing the bounciness values of two shapes to form a shape contact. This is assigned to the current Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape._surfaceMaterial.

Get/Set the Object that callbacks for the shapes owned by this chain will be sent to. Care should be taken with any Object assigned as a callback target that isn't a Object as this assignment will not in itself keep the object alive and can be garbage collected. To avoid this, you should have at least a single reference to the object in your code. To remove the object assigned here, set the callback target to NULL.
This includes the following events:
- A Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsEvents.ContactFilterEvent with call Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsCallbacks.IContactFilterCallback. - A Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsEvents.PreSolveEvent with call Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsCallbacks.IPreSolveCallback. - A Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsEvents.TriggerBeginEvent with call Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsCallbacks.ITriggerCallback. - A Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsEvents.TriggerEndEvent with call Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsCallbacks.ITriggerCallback. - A Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsEvents.ContactBeginEvent with call Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsCallbacks.IContactCallback. - A Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsEvents.ContactEndEvent with call Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsCallbacks.IContactCallback.
The friction of the owned chain shapes. Usually this is within the range [0, 1]. Values higher than 1 will result in energy being added which can lead to an unstable simulation.
Defines the method used when mixing the friction values of two shapes to form a shape contact. This is assigned to the current Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape._surfaceMaterial.

Get the number of geometries that were rejected during the last Geometry Composition. Geometry can be rejected for a number of reasons such as vertices being collinear or too close etc. Whilst "pure" geometry is always valid, this geometry is meant to be used by physics which has constraints on what it can accept. All geometry successfully created will always be valid when used by physics. If you notice thin/small gaps in the composition, this is likely to be rejected geometry. Checking this property will help determine that.

Get/Set if Delaunay tessellation is to be used. Delaunay tessellation is enabled by default and produces far superior results. Controls if worlds are always drawn independent of whether rendering is currently active or not as specified by Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._renderingMode. When true, world drawing is always active and a Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsEvents.WorldDrawResults event is produced containing the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.DrawResults. When false, world drawing only occurs depending on the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._renderingMode setting.
CAUTION: Drawing the world has a performance cost associated with it therefore when using this without rendering, that cost can become hidden.

Controls how many simulations can be started in parallel. Each one is started on its own worker and acts as its own main-thread. Workers should ideally be left free for the solver otherwise it may degrade solving performance. The actual quantity of workers used will always be capped to those available on the current device.
If the total number of workers available is below 4 then parallel simulation won't occur however parallel solving using workers will. This should not be confused with the quantity of workers used when solving a simulation. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorldDefinition._simulationWorkers.
The mode used for the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape.ContactFilter when determining if two Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape can contact. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape.ContactFilterGroupMode.

Controls the simulation of any Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld temporarily removing simulation overhead. When true, no automatic simulation will occur. When false, normal operation occurs with automatic simulation.

The internal length units per meter.
The physics system relates all length units on meters but you may need different units for your project. You can set this value to use different units but it should only be modified before any other calls to the physics system occur and only modified once. Changing this value after any physics object has been created can result in severe simulation instabilities.
Essentially there are some internal tolerances, such as how close two shapes need to be before they are considered to be touching or when two vertices of a hull are so close that they should be considered the same point. For example, internally a value of 5mm (0.005 meters) is used as a value tuned to work well with most situations with game-sized objects described in meters. If you decide to work in a different unit system (such as pixels) then 0.005 pixels is not a good value for this constant and would be too precise, leading to numerical problems, especially far from the origin. Instead you should determine roughly how many pixels you have per meter. For example, say you want 32 pixels per meter then you should set the lengthUnitsPerMeter to be 32.0f. Setting a value of (say) 32.05 would result in the 5mm being scaled up to 0.16 meters, which is a more reasonable value for determining if shapes are touching and hull vertices are too close.
A good rule of thumb is to pass the pixel height of your player character to this function, so if your player character is 32 pixels high, then pass 32 to this function. Then you may confidently use pixels for all the length values sent to the physics system. All length values returned from the physics system will also then naturally be in pixels because the physics system does not do any scaling internally, however, you are now responsible for creating appropriate values for gravity, density, and forces.

Get/Set the maximum number of worlds that can be created. The larger the number of worlds, the more memory that is initially allocated so care must be taken. Setting this value to one will reduce start-up memory usage to a minimum but will not allow any additional worlds to be created. The maximum value must be in the range of 1 to 1024. Any change will only be handled by Exiting Play mode in the Editor or restarting the player build.

member.name: M:Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsDestructor.Fragment(Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsDestructor/FragmentGeometry,System.ReadOnlySpan`1<UnityEngine.Vector2>,Unity.Collections.Allocator)

summary.para:
Fragment the specified target geometry using the specified fragment points.
The fragment points define areas where polygon fragments will be produced from the target geometry.
If the resulting polygon fragments have more polygon vertices than can fit into a single Unity.U2D.Physics.PolygonGeometry then the fragment will be split into multiple polygon fragments. The maximum number of vertices a single polygon fragment can have is defined by Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsConstants.MaxPolygonVertices.
If even a single fragment point overlaps the target geometry then all results will be returned in Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsDestructor.FragmentResult._brokenGeometry. If none of the fragment points overlap the target geometry then all the results will be returned in Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsDestructor.FragmentResult._unbrokenGeometry. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsDestructor.FragmentResult.

member.param: The target geometry to fragment. There must be at least a single geometry element. Any target polygons with a non-zero radius will be ignored.
The world-space fragment points used to define fragment regions. The number of fragment points must be greater than 1.
The memory allocator to use for the results. This can only be Allocator.Temp, Allocator.TempJob or Allocator.Persistent.

returns.para: The fragment results. These results must be disposed of after use otherwise leaks will occur.

member.name: M:Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsDestructor.Fragment(Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsDestructor/FragmentGeometry,Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsDestructor/FragmentGeometry,System.ReadOnlySpan`1<UnityEngine.Vector2>,Unity.Collections.Allocator)

summary.para:
Fragment the specified mask geometry using the specified fragment points, after the target geometry has the mask (carving) geometry removed from it.
The target geometry is first clipped with the mask geometry using a Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsComposer.Operation.NOT operation. The resulting target geometry is returned in Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsDestructor.FragmentResult._unbrokenGeometry. The mask geometry is then clipped with the original target geometry using an Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsComposer.Operation.AND operation. If the clipped mask produces no geometry then no results are returned in Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsDestructor.FragmentResult._brokenGeometry.
The fragment points define areas where polygon fragments will be produced from the clipped masked geometry. The resulting polygon fragments are returned in Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsDestructor.FragmentResult._brokenGeometry.
If the resulting polygon fragments have more polygon vertices than can fit into a single Unity.U2D.Physics.PolygonGeometry then the fragment will be split into multiple polygon fragments. The maximum number of vertices a single polygon fragment can have is defined by Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsConstants.MaxPolygonVertices. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsDestructor.FragmentResult.

member.param: The target geometry to fragment. There must be at least a single geometry element. Any target polygons with a non-zero radius will be ignored.

member.name: M:Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsDistanceJoint.SetOwner(UnityEngine.Object)

summary.para: Set the (optional) owner object associated with this joint and return an owner key that must be specified when destroying the joint with Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsJoint.Destroy. The physics system provides access to all objects, including the ability to destroy them so this feature can be used to stop accidental destruction of objects that are owned by other objects. You can only set the owner once, multiple attempts will produce a warning. The lifetime of the specified owner object is not linked to this joint i.e. this joint will still be owned by the owner object, even if it is destroyed. It is also valid to not specify an owner object (NULL) to simply gain an owner key however it can be useful, if simply for debugging purposes and discovery, to know which object is the owner.

member.param: The object that owns this joint. This can be NULL if not required.

returns.para: An owner key that must be passed to Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsJoint.Destroy when destroying the joint.

member.name: M:Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsDistanceJoint.SetOwner(UnityEngine.Object,System.Int32)

summary.para: Set the owner object using the specified owner key. You can only set the owner once, multiple attempts will produce a warning. This call does not bind the lifetime of the specified owner object, it is simply a reference. It is also valid to not specify an owner object (NULL) to simply gain an owner key however it can be useful, if simply for debugging purposes and discovery, to know which object is the owner.

member.param: The object that owns this key. This can be NULL if not required but is recommended as the key is formed in part by the hash-code of the owner object.
The owner key to be used. If zero then a new owner key is created. You can use Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.CreateOwnerKey for this value although any non-zero integer will work.

summary.para:
An abstract handle that can be used for custom purposes such as handling miscellaneous physics object types abstractly. You can create a handle with Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsHandle.Create or Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsHandle.CreateBatch. You can destroy a handle with Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsHandle.Destroy or Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsHandle.DestroyBatch.
You can also get a handle from one of the following physics objects: Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody._physicsHandleUnity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape._physicsHandleUnity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsChain._physicsHandleUnity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsJoint._physicsHandleUnity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsDistanceJoint._physicsHandleUnity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsFixedJoint._physicsHandleUnity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsHingeJoint._physicsHandleUnity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsIgnoreJoint._physicsHandleUnity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsRelativeJoint._physicsHandleUnity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsSliderJoint._physicsHandleUnity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWheelJoint._physicsHandle
NOTE: When retrieving the handle from another physics object, the object type is not encoded so that must be handled separately. Because of this, it's entirely possible for two handles to be equal, differing only by the type they came from so care must be taken or the object type explicitly stored against handles.
Get the handle generation.

member.name: M:Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsHingeJoint.SetOwner(UnityEngine.Object)

summary.para: Set the (optional) owner object associated with this joint and return an owner key that must be specified when destroying the joint with Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsJoint.Destroy. The physics system provides access to all objects, including the ability to destroy them so this feature can be used to stop accidental destruction of objects that are owned by other objects. You can only set the owner once, multiple attempts will produce a warning. The lifetime of the specified owner object is not linked to this joint i.e. this joint will still be owned by the owner object, even if it is destroyed. It is also valid to not specify an owner object (NULL) to simply gain an owner key however it can be useful, if simply for debugging purposes and discovery, to know which object is the owner.

member.name: M:Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsRelativeJoint.SetOwner(UnityEngine.Object)

summary.para: Set the (optional) owner object associated with this joint and return an owner key that must be specified when destroying the joint with Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsJoint.Destroy. The physics system provides access to all objects, including the ability to destroy them so this feature can be used to stop accidental destruction of objects that are owned by other objects. You can only set the owner once, multiple attempts will produce a warning. The lifetime of the specified owner object is not linked to this joint i.e. this joint will still be owned by the owner object, even if it is destroyed. It is also valid to not specify an owner object (NULL) to simply gain an owner key however it can be useful, if simply for debugging purposes and discovery, to know which object is the owner.

summary.para:
A shape is attached to a body and defines an area to which two distinct types of behaviour are handled:
- Collision: Contacts between shapes produce a collision response on their respective bodies, assuming their body type is Dynamic. - Trigger: Contacts between shapes do not produce a collision response, only the fact that they're overlapping is reported.
An unlimited number of shapes can be attached to a single body, known as a compound body. A shape is automatically destroyed when the body it is attached to is destroyed. A shape cannot exist unattached from a body.

Get the world AABB that bounds this shape. The bounds of the shape is inflated slightly due to speculative collision detection. The inflation is smaller on Static shape types however it is not zero due to time-of-impact collision detection. If an exact AABB is required then you can retrieve that via the shape geometry. See Unity.U2D.Physics.CircleGeometry.CalculateAABB, Unity.U2D.Physics.CapsuleGeometry.CalculateAABB, Unity.U2D.Physics.PolygonGeometry.CalculateAABB and Unity.U2D.Physics.SegmentGeometry.CalculateAABB.
The body which the shape is attached to.

The bounciness (coefficient of restitution) usually in the range [0, 1]. Values higher than 1 will result in energy being added which can lead to an unstable simulation. This is assigned to the current Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape._surfaceMaterial.
Defines the method used when mixing the friction values of two shapes to form a contact. This is assigned to the current Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape._surfaceMaterial.

The priority for combining the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape._bounciness properties when two shapes come into contact. If the priority of one shape is higher than the other shape then the higher priority Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape.SurfaceMaterial._bouncinessMixing will be used. If the priority of both shapes are the same then simply the higher enumeration value of PhysicsMaterialCombine2D from both shapes will be used. This is assigned to the current Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape._surfaceMaterial.

Get/Set the Object that callbacks for this shape will be sent to. Care should be taken with any Object assigned as a callback target that isn't a Object as this assignment will not in itself keep the object alive and can be garbage collected. To avoid this, you should have at least a single reference to the object in your code. To remove the object assigned here, set the callback target to NULL.
This includes the following events:
- A Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsEvents.ContactFilterEvent with call Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsCallbacks.IContactFilterCallback. - A Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsEvents.PreSolveEvent with call Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsCallbacks.IPreSolveCallback. - A Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsEvents.TriggerBeginEvent with call Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsCallbacks.ITriggerCallback. - A Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsEvents.TriggerEndEvent with call Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsCallbacks.ITriggerCallback. - A Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsEvents.ContactBeginEvent with call Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsCallbacks.IContactCallback. - A Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsEvents.ContactEndEvent with call Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsCallbacks.IContactCallback.

Get/Set the Capsule associated with this shape. When getting the shape geometry, the shape type must match the geometry type otherwise a warning will be produced and invalid geometry will be returned. Setting the geometry will change the type of shape represented even if the shape type was different before. Setting the geometry will also result in waking the body the shape is attached to.

Get the owning chain. The type of shape must be Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape.ShapeType.ChainSegment otherwise a warning will be produced. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape._isChainSegment and Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsChain.

Get/Set the Chain Segment associated with this shape. When getting the shape geometry, the shape type must match the geometry type otherwise a warning will be produced and invalid geometry will be returned. Setting the geometry will change the type of shape represented even if the shape type was different before. Setting the geometry will also result in waking the body the shape is attached to.

Get/Set the Circle associated with this shape. When getting the shape geometry, the shape type must match the geometry type otherwise a warning will be produced and invalid geometry will be returned. Setting the geometry will change the type of shape represented even if the shape type was different before. Setting the geometry will result in waking the body the shape is attached to.

Controls whether this shape produces contact events which can be retrieved after the simulation has completed. Any contact events can be used to call the assigned Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape._callbackTarget. A contact event is produced if either shapes involved have contactEvents enabled. A contact event will produce a Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsCallbacks.IContactCallback to the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape._callbackTarget for both shapes involved.
The filter used when determining what contacts this shape participates in.

Controls whether this shape produces contact filter callbacks. A contact filter callback allows direct control over whether a contact will be created between a pair of shapes. This applies to both triggers and non-triggers but only with to Dynamic bodies These are relatively expensive so disabling them can provide a significant performance benefit. A contact filter callback will call the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape._callbackTarget for both shapes involved if they implement Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsCallbacks.IContactFilterCallback.

Custom debug draw color. Any color value other than Color._clear (RGBA=0) will be used to render the shape.. This value is passed back when using the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld drawing. The alpha value here is always ignored. This is assigned to the current Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape._surfaceMaterial.

Get/Set a shape definition by accessing all of its current properties. This is provided as convenience only and should not be used when performance is important as all the properties defined in the definition are accessed sequentially. You should try to only use the specific properties you need rather than using this feature.
The Coulomb (dry) friction coefficient, usually in the range [0, 1]. This is assigned to the current Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape._surfaceMaterial.
Defines the method used when mixing the friction values of two shapes to form a contact. This is assigned to the current Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape._surfaceMaterial.

The priority for combining the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape._friction properties when two shapes come into contact. If the priority of one shape is higher than the other shape then the higher priority Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape.SurfaceMaterial._frictionMixing will be used. If the priority of both shapes are the same then simply the higher enumeration value of PhysicsMaterialCombine2D from both shapes will be used. This is assigned to the current Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape._surfaceMaterial.
Controls whether this shape produces hit events which can be retrieved after the simulation has completed.
Check if the shape is a Chain type. A Chain type is owned by a chain. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape._chain and Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsChain.
Get if the shape is owned. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape.SetOwner.
Get/Set if the shape is a trigger. Changing the state here is relatively expensive and should be avoided. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShapeDefinition._isTrigger.
Check if the shape is valid.
Get the center of the shape, in local-space.

The shape mass configuration. Normally this only used on a body where the total of all shapes is used. This allows the calculation of this specific shape in isolation. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody.MassConfiguration.
The mover data for the shape mover.
Get Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsUserData that can be used for any purpose, typically by the owner only.
Get the physics handle.

Get/Set the Polygon associated with this shape. When getting the shape geometry, the shape type must match the geometry type otherwise a warning will be produced and invalid geometry will be returned. Setting the geometry will change the type of shape represented even if the shape type was different before. Setting the geometry will also result in waking the body the shape is attached to.

Controls whether this shape produces pre-solve callbacks. This only applies to Dynamic bodies and is ignored for triggers. These are relatively expensive so disabling them can provide a significant performance benefit. A pre-solve callback will call the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape._callbackTarget for both shapes involved if they implement Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsCallbacks.IPreSolveCallback.
The rolling resistance usually in the range [0, 1]. This is assigned to the current Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape._surfaceMaterial.

Get/Set the Segment associated with this shape. When getting the shape geometry, the shape type must match the geometry type otherwise a warning will be produced and invalid geometry will be returned. Setting the geometry will change the type of shape represented even if the shape type was different before. Setting the geometry will also result in waking the body the shape is attached to.
The type of shape. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape.ShapeType.

Should the body update its mass properties when this shape is created. Disabling this improves performance when multiple shapes are being added to the same body. The mass of a body can then be explicitly updated by calling Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody.ApplyMassFromShapes
See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShapeDefinition._startMassUpdate.

Normally shapes on Static bodies don't create contacts when they are added to the world. This overrides that behavior and causes contact creation. This significantly slows down Static body creation which can be important when there are many Static shapes. This is implicitly always true for Triggers, Dynamic bodies and Kinematic bodies.
See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShapeDefinition._startStaticContacts.

The surface material for the shape comprising of many properties such as friction, bounciness, rolling resistance etc. Setting the surface material overrides any individual settings for friction, bounciness, rolling resistance etc.
The tangent (surface) speed. This is assigned to the current Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape._surfaceMaterial.
Get the shape transform. This is simply the body transform. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody._transform.

Controls whether this shape produces triggers events which can be retrieved after the simulation has completed. A trigger event is only produced if both shapes involved have their triggerEvents enabled. A trigger event will produce a Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsCallbacks.ITriggerCallback to the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape._callbackTarget for both shapes involved.
Get/Set Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsUserData that can be used for any purpose. The physics system doesn't use this data, it is entirely for custom use.
Get the world the shape is attached to.
Controls whether this shape is automatically drawn when the world is drawn.

This also considers the relative velocity of the shape. This only has an effect if the shape body is RigidbodyType2D.Dynamic. This only has an effect of shapes of type Circle, Capsule or Polygon.

A contact filter is used to control what contacts are created when intersecting other shapes. A contact filter contains a filter with the addition of a group index allowing overrides to the filter.
See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape.ContactFilterMode.
The categories this object is in. Usually you would only set one bit but multiple are allowed.
The categories this object will produce contacts with.

member.name: M:Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape.ContactFilter.#ctor

summary.para: Create a contact filter. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape.ContactFilterMode.

member.param: A Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsMask defining the categories this object is in.
A Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsMask defining the categories this object will produce contacts with.
The group index this filter belongs to. How this is used is determined by Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape.ContactFilterGroupMode.

summary.para: The default categories used.
The default contacts used.
Get a contact filter that is all categories and contacts everything.
The mode used to determine how Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape.ContactFilter._groupIndex is used.

In this mode, the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape.ContactFilter._groupIndex is used to filter if contacts are allowed to be created by the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape.ContactFilter._categories and Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape.ContactFilter._contacts masks.
The rules for two shapes coming into contact are:
- If both shapes have an identical group then the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape.ContactFilter._categories and Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape.ContactFilter._contacts masks are used. - If both shapes have a different group then they will never produce a contact irrelevant of the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape.ContactFilter._categories and Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape.ContactFilter._contacts mask configuration. - A group of zero is used like any other group but is also the default therefore if unchanged, the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape.ContactFilter._categories and Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape.ContactFilter._contacts masks are used by default.

In this mode, the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape.ContactFilter._groupIndex is used to control if contacts are never created (negative) or always created (positive). A non-zero group always overrides the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape.ContactFilter._categories and Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape.ContactFilter._contacts masks. A group of zero has no effect.
The rules for two shapes coming into contact are:
- If either shape has a group of zero then the group is ignored and the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape.ContactFilter._categories and Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape.ContactFilter._contacts masks are used. - If both shapes have a non-zero but different group then the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape.ContactFilter._categories and Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape.ContactFilter._contacts masks are used. - If both shapes have an identical and positive group then they will always produce a contact. - If both shapes have an identical and negative group then they will never produce a contact.
The mode used for the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape.ContactFilter when determining if two Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape can contact. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsCoreSettings2D._contactFilterMode.

This mode will produce a contact if both Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape agree, effectively an AND operation. A contact will be produced if the following is true: (contactFilterA.contacts AND-MASK contactFilterB.categories) AND (contactFilterA.categories AND-MASK contactFilterB.contacts). How the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape.ContactFilter._groupIndex is used is determined by Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape.ContactFilterGroupMode.

This mode will produce a contact if either Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape agree, effectively an OR operation. A contact will be produced if the following is true: (contactFilterA.contacts AND-MASK contactFilterB.categories ) OR (contactFilterA.categories AND-MASK contactFilterB.contacts). How the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape.ContactFilter._groupIndex is used is determined by Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape.ContactFilterGroupMode.
The unique Id of the contact. This contact is volatile and may be destroyed automatically when the world is modified or simulated therefore it should always be checked for validity.
Get the contact.
Check if the contact is valid or not.
A contact manifold describes the contact points between colliding shapes. Speculative collision is used so some contact points may be separated, a property available per-contact.
The unit normal vector in world space, points from shape A to bodyB
The number of manifold points available, in the range [0, 2].
The manifold points, up to two are possible.
Angular impulse applied for rolling resistance (N " m " s = kg * m^2 / s).
The number of manifold points available that are speculative, in the range [0, 2].

Contains all the detail related to the geometry and dynamics of the contact. You may use the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape.ContactManifold.ManifoldPoint._totalNormalImpulse to determine if there was an interaction during the time step.
Location of the contact point relative to shapeA's origin in world space.
Location of the contact point relative to shapeB's origin in world space.
Uniquely identifies a contact point between two shapes. This should not be confused with Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape.ContactId.
The impulse along the manifold normal vector.
Relative normal velocity pre-solve. Used for hit events. If the normal impulse is zero then there was no hit. Negative means shapes are approaching.
Did this contact point exist the previous step?

Location of the contact point in world space. Subject to precision loss at large coordinates. This point lags behind when contact recycling is used. Preference should be to use anchorA and/or anchorB for game logic. This is also known as the "clip" point.
The separation of the contact point, negative if penetrating.
Is the contact point speculative i.e. not currently interacting?
The friction impulse.

The total normal impulse applied across sub-stepping and restitution. This includes the warm starting impulse, the sub-step delta impulse, and the restitution impulse. This can be used to identify speculative contact points that had an interaction during the simulation step.
Fixed-sized manifold point array.
Manifold Point #0.
Manifold Point #1.
The number of manifold points available that are speculative, in the range [0, 2].

If the object is owned with Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape.SetOwner then you must provide the owner key it returned. Failing to do so will return a warning and the shape will not be destroyed. summary.para: The type of shape. Some shapes are "closed" meaning they have an interior which will produce contacts. Some shapes are "open" meaning they do not have an interior and will only produce contacts when their boundary is intersected.
A capsule is an extruded circle. This is a closed shape. See Unity.U2D.Physics.CapsuleGeometry.

A Chain of line segments that are joined together with other line segments. This is an open shape. This is indirectly created and owned by a chain. See Unity.U2D.Physics.ChainSegmentGeometry and Unity.U2D.Physics.ChainGeometry.
A circle with an offset. This is a closed shape. See Unity.U2D.Physics.CircleGeometry.
A convex polygon. This is a closed shape. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PolygonGeometry.
A line segment. This is an open shape. See Unity.U2D.Physics.SegmentGeometry.
Defines the dynamics of a surface on a shape.
The bounciness (coefficient of restitution) usually in the range [0, 1].
Defines the method used when mixing the bounciness values of two shapes to form a contact.

The priority for mixing the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape._bounciness properties when two shapes come into contact. If the priority of one shape is higher than the other shape then the higher priority Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape.SurfaceMaterial._bouncinessMixing will be used. If the priority of both shapes are the same then simply the higher enumeration value of Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape.SurfaceMaterial.MixingMode from both shapes will be used.

Custom debug draw color. Any color value other than (0,0,0,0) will be used to render the shape. This value is passed back when using the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld drawing. The alpha value here is always ignored.
Get the default surface material.
The Coulomb (dry) friction coefficient, usually in the range [0, 1].
Defines the method used when mixing the friction values of two shapes to form a contact.

The priority for mixing the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape._friction properties when two shapes come into contact. If the priority of one shape is higher than the other shape then the higher priority Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape.SurfaceMaterial._frictionMixing will be used. If the priority of both shapes are the same then simply the higher enumeration value of Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape.SurfaceMaterial.MixingMode from both shapes will be used.
The rolling resistance usually in the range [0, 1].
The tangent (surface) speed.
Create a default surface material.

The average of both surface values.
The maximum of both surface values.
The geometric mean of both surface values.
The minium of both surface values.
The product of both surface values.
A Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape definition used to specify important initial properties.

Controls whether this shape produces contact events which can be retrieved after the simulation has completed. This only applies to kinematic and dynamic bodies. A contact event is produced if either shapes involved have their contactEvents enabled. Changing this at run-time may lead to lost begin/end events.
The contact filter used to control which contacts this shape can participate in.

Controls whether this shape produces contact filter callbacks. A contact filter callback allows direct control over whether a contact will be created between a pair of shapes. This applies to both triggers and non-triggers but only with to Dynamic bodies These are relatively expensive so disabling them can provide a significant performance benefit. A contact filter callback will call the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape._callbackTarget for both shapes involved if they implement Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsCallbacks.IContactFilterCallback.
Get a default Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape definition.
The density, usually in kg/m^2, defaults to 1. This is not part of the surface material because this is for the interior of the shape, which may have other considerations, such as being hollow.
Controls whether this shape produces hit events which can be retrieved after the simulation has completed. This only applies to kinematic and dynamic bodies. This is ignored for triggers.

Enable/Disable being a trigger shape. A trigger shape generates overlap events but never generates a collision response. Triggers do not collide with other triggers and do not have continuous collision, instead, use a ray or shape cast for those scenarios. Triggers still contribute to the body mass if they have non-zero density. The default is false.
The mover data used for the shape mover.

Controls whether this shape produces pre-solve callbacks. This only applies to Dynamic bodies and is ignored for triggers. These are relatively expensive so disabling them can provide a significant performance benefit. A pre-solve callback will call the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape._callbackTarget for both shapes involved if they implement Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsCallbacks.IPreSolveCallback.

Should the body update its mass properties when this shape is created. Disabling this improves performance when multiple shapes are being added to the same body. The mass of a body can then be explicitly updated by calling Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody.ApplyMassFromShapes
See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape._startMassUpdate.

Normally shapes on Static bodies don't create contacts when they are added to the world. This overrides that behavior and causes contact creation. This significantly slows down Static body creation which can be important when there are many Static shapes. This is implicitly always true for Triggers, Dynamic bodies and Kinematic bodies.
See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape._startStaticContacts.
The surface material for the shape comprising of many properties such as friction, bounciness, rolling resistance etc.

Controls whether this shape produces trigger events which can be retrieved after the simulation has completed. A trigger event is only produced if both shapes involved have their triggerEvents enabled. This applies to triggers and non-triggers alike.

Controls whether this shape is automatically drawn when the world is drawn.
See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape._worldDrawing.
Create a default Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape definition.

member.name: M:Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsSliderJoint.SetOwner(UnityEngine.Object)

summary.para: Set the (optional) owner object associated with this joint and return an owner key that must be specified when destroying the joint with Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsJoint.Destroy. The physics system provides access to all objects, including the ability to destroy them so this feature can be used to stop accidental destruction of objects that are owned by other objects. You can only set the owner once, multiple attempts will produce a warning. The lifetime of the specified owner object is not linked to this joint i.e. this joint will still be owned by the owner object, even if it is destroyed. It is also valid to not specify an owner object (NULL) to simply gain an owner key however it can be useful, if simply for debugging purposes and discovery, to know which object is the owner.

member.param: The object that owns this joint. This can be NULL if not required.

returns.para: An owner key that must be passed to Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsJoint.Destroy when destroying the joint.

summary.para: A world is a container for all other physics objects such as Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody, Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape, Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsJoint etc. A world can be simulated in isolation from all other worlds. The maximum number of worlds that can be created at one time is defined by Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsCoreSettings2D._maximumWorlds. A world is completely isolated from all other worlds.

Get the distance used to expand AABBs in the broadphase dynamic tree, in meters. This allows broadphase proxies to move by a small amount without triggering a tree adjustment. This value is 0.05f * Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._lengthUnitsPerMeter. Normally this is 5cm.

Get if worlds are always drawn independent of whether rendering is currently active or not as specified by Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._renderingMode. When true, world drawing is always active and a Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsEvents.WorldDrawResults event is produced containing the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.DrawResults. When false, world drawing only occurs depending on the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._renderingMode setting. This can be controlled via Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsCoreSettings2D._alwaysDrawWorlds.
Controls if body update callback targets are automatically called. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.SendBodyUpdateCallbacks
Controls if shape contact callback targets are automatically called. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.SendContactCallbacks
Controls if joint threshold callback targets are automatically called. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.SendJointThresholdCallbacks
Controls if shape trigger callback targets are automatically called. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.SendTriggerCallbacks
Get the number of awake bodies in the world.

Get the maximum rotation of a body per time step, in degrees. This limit is very large and is used to prevent numerical problems. This value is approximately 45-degrees or 0.25f * Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsMath.PI radians.
Get the time that a body must be still before it will go to sleep, in seconds. This value is 0.5 seconds.

Get the body events from the last simulation. The Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody objects returned should be checked to see if they are valid before accessing as they may have been deleted since this event was produced (see Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody._isValid). Any change to the world state can invalidate this data so referring to this data afterwards may cause an unavoidable crash! You must immediately extract what information you need and not directly reference the returned data as it will be cleared immediately after being provided. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsEvents.BodyUpdateEvent.
Adjust the bounce threshold, usually in meters per second. It is recommended not to make this value very small because it will prevent bodies from sleeping.

Get the current world capacities reached since the world was created. This reflects the peak object counts and can be used to presize a Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorldDefinition._capacity for similar worlds. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorldDefinition._capacity.

Gets how many simulations can be started in parallel.
Whilst running simulations in parallel can improver overall performance, workers should ideally be left free for the simulation solver otherwise it may degrade solving performance. The actual quantity of workers used will always be capped to those available on the current device. If the total number of workers available is below 4 then parallel simulation won't occur as generally this would reduce overall performance, however parallel solving of each simulation using workers will still be used. This should not be confused with the quantity of workers used when solving a simulation.

Get the contact begin events from the last simulation. The Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape objects returned should be checked to see if they are valid before accessing as they may have been deleted since this event was produced (see Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape._isValid). The Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape.Contact objects returned should be checked to see if they are valid before accessing as they may have been deleted since this event was produced. Any change to the world state can invalidate this data so referring to this data afterwards may cause an unavoidable crash! You must immediately extract what information you need and not directly reference the returned data as it will be cleared immediately after being provided. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsEvents.ContactBeginEvent.
The contact bounciness with 1 being critical damping (non-dimensional).

Get the contact end events from the last simulation. The Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape objects returned should be checked to see if they are valid before accessing as they may have been deleted since this event was produced (see Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape._isValid). The Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape.Contact objects returned should be checked to see if they are valid before accessing as they may have been deleted since this event was produced. Any change to the world state can invalidate this data so referring to this data afterwards may cause an unavoidable crash! You must immediately extract what information you need and not directly reference the returned data as it will be cleared immediately after being provided. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsEvents.ContactEndEvent.

Controls if contact filter callbacks will be called. A contact filter callback allows direct control over whether a contact will be created between a pair of shapes. This applies to both triggers and non-triggers but only with Dynamic bodies. These are relatively expensive so disabling them can provide a significant performance benefit. A contact filter callback will call the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape._callbackTarget for both shapes involved if they implement Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsCallbacks.IContactFilterCallback.
Get the current value of Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsCoreSettings2D._contactFilterGroupMode.
Get the current value of Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsCoreSettings2D._contactFilterMode.
The contact stiffness, in cycles per second.

Get the contact hit events from the last simulation. The Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape objects returned should be checked to see if they are valid before accessing as they may have been deleted since this event was produced (see Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape._isValid). Any change to the world state can invalidate this data so referring to this data afterwards may cause an unavoidable crash! You must immediately extract what information you need and not directly reference the returned data as it will be cleared immediately after being provided.
