The contact hit event threshold controls the collision speed needed to generate a contact hit event, usually in meters per second. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsEvents.ContactHitEvent.

The contact recycle distance, in meters. Setting this to zero disables contact point recycling. Contact recycling reuses contact points across simulation time-steps when the relative movement is small. This feature improves stability and performance by around 25% (approximately). Contact points are not recalculated until shapes move more than 5cm (default) relative to each other. Contact recycling skips some updates such as friction, pre-solve (etc) until the contacts are no longer recycled.
The contact speed used to solve overlaps, in meters per second.

Controls if continuous collision detection will be used between Dynamic and Static bodies. Generally you should keep continuous collision enabled to prevent fast moving objects from going through Static objects. The performance gain from disabling continuous collision is minor.
Get the world counters.

Get the default world created at start-up. This world cannot be destroyed as it is permanently owned by Unity itself. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.SetOwner and Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._isOwned.

Get/Set a world definition by accessing all of its current properties. This is provided as convenience only and should not be used when performance is important as all the properties defined in the definition are accessed sequentially. You should try to only use the specific properties you need rather than using this feature.

Get if the automatic simulation of any Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld is temporarily disabled. When true, no automatic simulation will occur. When false, normal operation occurs with automatic simulation. This can be controlled via Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsCoreSettings2D._disableSimulation.
Controls what colors are used to draw Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody, Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape, Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsJoint etc.
Controls the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.DrawContactType used when drawing contact points.

Controls the draw fill alpha. This is used to scale the interior fill alpha and is only used when Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.DrawFillOptions.Outline is used so that the interior color can be distinguished from the outline color by transparency.
Controls how shape geometry is filled when drawing. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.DrawFillOptions.

Limits what gets drawn to a narrow selection. This only affects Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.DrawOptions that are drawing all bodies, shapes etc. It does not affect selected elements or custom drawing. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.IgnoreFilter.
Controls the joint contact force scale used when drawing contact forces.
Controls the joint contact normal scale used when drawing contact normals.
Limits what gets drawn to a broad selection. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.DrawOptions.
Controls the draw point scale used when drawing points.
Controls the draw thickness (outline and orientation).

Controls the element depth.
When using custom drawing of geometry or primitive shapes there is no reference to the orthogonal axis used with respect to the current Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._transformPlane.
The element depth is in world-space and for each transform plan is defined as:
- Element depth is rendered along the Z axis when using Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.TransformPlane.XY. - Element depth is rendered along the Y axis when using Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.TransformPlane.XZ. - Element depth is rendered along the X axis when using Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.TransformPlane.ZY.
You should set the element depth before performing any custom draw.
The element depth will be reset to zero when rendering is complete.
Get the world handle generation.
Get the world counters, summed for all the active worlds.
Get the world timing profile, summed for all the active worlds.
GetSet the gravity vector applied to all bodies in the world, usually in ms^2.

Gets what physics considers a large extent in the world. Positions greater than approximately 16km will have precision problems, so 100km as a limit should be fine in all cases. This is used to detect bad values. This value is 100000.0f * Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._lengthUnitsPerMeter.
Get the world handle index.
Check if this is the default Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld. The default world is automatically created at start-up.
Check if the world is empty as defined by having no bodies, shapes or joints.
Get if the world is owned. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.SetOwner.
Get if rendering is currently allowed. Rendering is always allowed in the Editor however it is only allowed elsewhere depending on Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsCoreSettings2D._renderingMode.
Check if the world is valid.

Get the joint events from the last simulation. An event is produced by a Joint which exceeds either its Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsJoint._forceThreshold or Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsJoint._torqueThreshold. The Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsJoint objects returned should be checked to see if they are valid before accessing as they may have been deleted since this event was produced (see Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsJoint._isValid). Any change to the world state can invalidate this data so referring to this data afterwards may cause an unavoidable crash! You must immediately extract what information you need and not directly reference the returned data as it will be cleared immediately after being provided. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsEvents.JointThresholdEvent.
Get the delta-time used for the last simulation run.
Get the timestamp when the last simulation was run.

Get the internal length units per meter. Changes won't take effect until exiting play mode. The physics system relates all length units on meters but you may need different units for your project. You can set this value to use different units but it should only be modified before any other calls to the physics system occur and only modified once. Changing this value after any physics object has been created can result in severe simulation instabilities.
For example, if your game uses pixels for units you can use pixels for all length values sent to the physics system. There should be no extra cost however, the physics system has some internal tolerances and thresholds that have been tuned for meters. By calling this function, the physics system is better able to adjust those tolerances and thresholds to improve accuracy. A good rule of thumb is to pass the height of your player character to this function. So if your player character is 32 pixels high, then pass 32 to this function. Then you may confidently use pixels for all the length values sent to the physics system. All length values returned from the physics system will also then be in pixels because the physics system does not do any scaling internally, however, you are now on the hook for coming up with good values for gravity, density, and forces.
The default value is 1.

Get the small length used as a collision and constraint tolerance, in meters. Usually it is chosen to be numerically significant, but visually insignificant. This value is 0.005f * Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._lengthUnitsPerMeter. Normally this is 0.5cm.
Get/Set the maximum linear speed.

Get the actual allocated maximum worlds available. This can differ at runtime from Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsCoreSettings2D._maximumWorlds if it was changed and the physics system has not been restarted. Another reason this can differ would be if there was not available memory to allocate the requested maximum worlds.
Get Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsUserData that can be used for any purpose, typically by the owner only.
Get/Set if the world is paused. When paused, any simulation attempted will be ignored whether it be automatic or manual.

Controls if pre-solve callbacks will be called. This only applies to Dynamic bodies and is ignored for triggers. These are relatively expensive so disabling them can provide a significant performance benefit. A pre-solve callback will call the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape._callbackTarget for both shapes involved if they implement Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsCallbacks.IPreSolveCallback.
Get the world timing profile.

Get the current value of Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsCoreSettings2D._renderingMode.
NOTE: Drawing and rendering are always available in the Unity Editor however rendering requires compute buffer support on any device it is used without which no rendering will occur.

Get/Set whether safety threading locks are enabled or not. Locks are enabled by default however on platforms that do not support threading, locks are not used. Disabling locks can result in a small performance boost however, please note the following EXTREME CAUTIONS.
Typically, per-world, multiple read operations can happen in parallel however only a single write operation can occur concurrently.
Read and write operations can never happen at the same time. Locking is a self-balancing reader-preferred system that tries to reduce writers "starving". Once a writer is in a queue, it registers incoming readers as waiting readers and, once active readers are handled, it starts processing a single writer. After that writer has been handled, it flips waiting readers into active readers and processes them. Whilst this system is extremely fast, it does have a very small overhead. Disabling this system can give a small performance boost but is nearly always not worth it therefore this option should be used for testing only.
EXTREME CAUTION should be taken if disabling locks on platforms that support threading! A majority of this API is thread-safe and is is due to the safety locks! Locks are used to ensure that read and write operations do not interfere with each other. Locks also ensure that no read or write operations happen during a simulation step. Overlapping read or write operations will almost certainly result in corruptions and a subsequent crash, so unless you are absolutely sure this is not the case, do not disable locks!
Get/Set the simulation sub-steps to use during simulation. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.Simulate.
Get/Set the simulation type which controls when or if the simulation will be automatically simulated. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.SimulationType.

Get/Set the simulation worker count for the world. A single simulation worker is always used for simulation therefore a worker count of one means single thread simulation only. The actual quantity of workers used will always be capped to those available on the current device and reading the property will return the number of workers actually being used by the device. Changing the worker count continuously is not recommend and will impact performance as it requires the task queue be recreated. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorldDefinition._simulationWorkers.
Controls if bodies go to sleep when not moving and not interacting. Sleeping can provide a significant performance improvement when many Dynamic or Kinematic bodies are in the world.
Get the distance at which speculative contacts will be calculated. This reduces jitter. This value is 4.0f * Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._lengthUnitsPerMeter. Normally this is 2cm.

Controls if an extra write pass prior to the script fixed-update callback is made for any interpolation tweens to ensure that transforms are synchronized to the final body pose. Because this is an extra write pass, it has an impact on overall performance so only enable if you require transforms synchronized this way.
NOTE: This only affects Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody that have their Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody._transformWriteMode set to Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody.TransformWriteMode.Interpolate.
Get the current value of Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsCoreSettings2D._transformChangeMode. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.TransformChangeMode.
Controls the transform plane that the world uses when writing transforms. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._transformWriteMode.

Controls the transformation for the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.TransformPlane.Custom to allow transformation writing and reading to/from a custom 2D plane. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.TransformPlaneCustom.

Controls if and how Transform tweens are calculated and/or written. Transform tweening is where bodies that have their Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody._transformObject set, write to the Transform each frame depending on the specific body Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody.TransformWriteMode set. Regardless of this setting, Transform tweening is never used if the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._simulationType is Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.SimulationType.Update or Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._transformWriteMode is Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.TransformWriteMode.Off.

Get/Set the custom Object that implements the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsCallbacks.ITransformWriteCallback to which Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsEvents.TransformWriteEvent and Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsEvents.TransformTweenWriteEvent will be sent. The callback will only occur if Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._transformWriteMode is set to Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.TransformWriteMode.Custom and there are Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._bodyUpdateEvents available. The object assigned here will be kept alive, not allowing the GC to dispose of it. To remove the object assigned here, set the callback target to NULL.

Controls how transform writing is handled. Only bodies that have their Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody._transformWriteMode active and produce a Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsEvents.BodyUpdateEvent will write to a transform. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.TransformWriteMode.

Get the trigger begin events from the last simulation. The Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape objects returned should be checked to see if they are valid before accessing as they may have been deleted since this event was produced (see Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape._isValid). Any change to the world state can invalidate this data so referring to this data afterwards may cause an unavoidable crash! You must immediately extract what information you need and not directly reference the returned data as it will be cleared immediately after being provided. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsEvents.TriggerBeginEvent.

Get the trigger end events from the last simulation. The Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape objects returned should be checked to see if they are valid before accessing as they may have been deleted since this event was produced (see Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape._isValid). Any change to the world state can invalidate this data so referring to this data afterwards may cause an unavoidable crash! You must immediately extract what information you need and not directly reference the returned data as it will be cleared immediately after being provided. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsEvents.TriggerEndEvent.

Get if the option of Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsCoreSettings2D._usePhysicsLayers is active or not. If no Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsCoreSettings2D asset is assigned, this option will return false (inactive). When active, the physics 64-bit layers are used (see Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsCoreSettings2D._physicsLayerNames) for property drawers and Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsLayers.GetLayerMask. When inactive, the 32-bit layers are used (see LayerMask) for property drawers and Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsLayers.GetLayerMask. In all cases, the physics system itself will always use the full 64-bit layers assigned, however when using 32-bit layers, the top 32-bits will be set to zero.

Get/Set Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsUserData that can be used for any purpose. This cannot be set on the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._defaultWorld and will always be at the default. The physics system doesn't use this data, it is entirely for custom use.
Is warm-starting allowed in the world? Disabling warming-starting will severely impact stability. This is typically used for testing only!
Get the number of created worlds. This will be a value in the range of 1 to Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsCoreSettings2D._maximumWorlds.

summary.para: Get the owner object associated with this world as specified using Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.SetOwner.

returns.para: The owner object associated with this world or NULL if no owner has been specified.

summary.para:
Gets all the existing Transform Write Tweens that are handled per-frame. If the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._transformTweenMode is Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.TransformTweenMode.Sequential then the tweens are sorted into ascending transform depth allowing writing to the Transform hierarchy by simply iterating the tweens . If the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._transformTweenMode is Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.TransformTweenMode.Sequential then the tweens are unsorted as a Jobs.TransformAccessArray is used to write them. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody.TransformWriteTween and Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody.TransformWriteMode.
The returned Collections.NativeArray_1 aliases the per-frame internal buffer owned by the world; it does not own its memory (so disposing it does nothing). The contents are only valid until the next simulation step runs, after which the buffer may be reused or destroyed. If a longer-lived copy is required, copy the contents into a caller-owned Collections.NativeArray_1.

returns.para: A world-owned view of the existing Transform Write Tweens that are handled per-frame. Contents are invalidated by the next simulation step.

See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsAABB, Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsQuery.QueryFilter, Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsQuery.WorldOverlapResult and Collections.Allocator.

member.param: The AABB used to check overlap. This must be in world-space.
The filter to control what results are returned.
The memory allocator to use for the results. This can only be Allocator.Temp, Allocator.TempJob or Allocator.Persistent.

returns.para: The query overlap results. This NativeArray must be disposed of after use otherwise leaks will occur. The exception to this is if the array is empty.

member.name: M:Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.RegisterTransformChange(UnityEngine.Transform,Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsCallbacks/ITransformChangedCallback)

summary.para:
Register a transform watcher to call the specified callback when a transform changes. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsEvents.TransformChangeEvent for the types of transform changes that are watched for.
You MUST unregister this when no longer needed with Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.UnregisterTransformChange otherwise you will receive warnings.

member.param: The transform to watch for changes.
The callback to perform when a transform change is detected.

summary.para:
Controls drawing and rendering is allowed.
NOTE: Drawing and rendering are always available in the Unity Editor however rendering requires compute buffer support on any device it is used without which no rendering will occur.
Drawing and rendering is available in the Editor and any player build.
Drawing and rendering is available in both the Editor and a Development player build.
Drawing and rendering is only available in the Editor and not in a player build.
Reset the world to a canonical state so that it will reproduce identical results each time. The world must be empty for this to be called otherwise a warning is produced.

Send all callbacks to targets:
- Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.SendBodyUpdateCallbacks - Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.SendTriggerCallbacks - Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.SendContactCallbacks - Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.SendJointThresholdCallbacks

Send all current Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._bodyUpdateEvents where the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody involved are valid (see Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody._isValid) and have a callback target assigned (see Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody._callbackTarget). Only callback targets that implement Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsCallbacks.IBodyUpdateCallback will be called. This will be called automatically if Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._autoBodyUpdateCallbacks is true. This must be called on the main thread.

Send all current Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._contactBeginEvents and Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._contactEndEvents where either of the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape involved are valid (see Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape._isValid) and have a callback target assigned (see Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape._callbackTarget). These events will only be created if both of the shape pairs has Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape._contactEvents set to true. Only callback targets that implement Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsCallbacks.IContactCallback will be called. This will be called automatically if Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._autoContactCallbacks is true. This must be called on the main thread.

Send all current Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._jointThresholdEvents where the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsJoint involved are valid (see Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsJoint._isValid) and have a callback target assigned (see Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsJoint._callbackTarget). These events will only be created if the joint exceeds its Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsJoint._forceThreshold or Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsJoint._torqueThreshold. Only callback targets that implement Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsCallbacks.IJointThresholdCallback will be called. This will be called automatically if Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._autoJointThresholdCallbacks is true. This must be called on the main thread.

Send all current Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._triggerBeginEvents and Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._triggerEndEvents where either of the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape involved are valid (see Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape._isValid) and have a callback target assigned (see Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape._callbackTarget). These events will only be created if one of the shape pairs has Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape._triggerEvents set to true. Only callback targets that implement Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsCallbacks.ITriggerCallback will be called. This will be called automatically if Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._autoTriggerCallbacks is true. This must be called on the main thread.

summary.para: Set the owner object using the specified owner key. You can only set the owner once, multiple attempts will produce a warning. member.name: M:Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.SetOwner(UnityEngine.Object,System.Int32)

summary.para: Set the owner object using the specified owner key. You can only set the owner once, multiple attempts will produce a warning. This call does not bind the lifetime of the specified owner object, it is simply a reference. It is also valid to not specify an owner object (NULL) to simply gain an owner key however it can be useful, if simply for debugging purposes and discovery, to know which object is the owner.

summary.para:
Defines when changes to Transform that are registered with Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.RegisterTransformChange are called.
NOTE: In the Unity Editor when not in Play Mode, Transform change callbacks are always and only sent at the start of the frame for authoring purposes.

Transform Change callbacks are sent after the "FixedUpdate" script callbacks but before any "FixedUpdate" simulation(s). This is typically used when any changes to Transforms occur in the "FixedUpdate" script callbacks need to be handled before any "FixedUpdate" simulation(s).

Transform Change callbacks are sent at the start of a frame prior to the "FixedUpdate" or "Update" script callbacks. This is typically used when any changes to Transform from the previous frame need to be handled before anything else runs.
Transform Change callbacks are not sent in play mode.

Transform Change callbacks are sent after the "Update" script callbacks but before any "Update" simulation(s). This is typically used when any changes to Transforms during the "Update" script callbacks need to be handled before any "Update" simulation(s).

Defines the reason why a Transform changed. Register and unregister for transform changes with Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.RegisterTransformChange and Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.UnregisterTransformChange.
The animation system wrote a physics-based world-space TRS change.
Any transform change.
The local position, rotation or scale of the transform changed.
The world-space position, rotation or scale of the transform changed.
The local position of the transform changed. This does not propagate to children or parent transforms. See Transform._localPosition.
The local rotation of the transform changed. This does not propagate to children or parent transforms. See Transform._localRotation.
The local scale of the transform changed. This does not propagate to children or parent transforms. See Transform._localScale.
The parent transform hierarchy changed. Indicates that a direct or indirect parent has been added, removed or re-parented.
The World-space position of the transform changed. Changing a parent results in an event in children transform too. See Transform._position.
The World-space rotation of the transform changed. Changing a parent results in an event in children transform too. See Transform._rotation.
The World-space scale of the transform changed. Changing a parent results in an event in children transform too. See Transform._lossyScale.

summary.para: Defines if and how Transform tweens are calculated and/or written.

Transform tweens are not calculated or written. Instead, the callback target set with Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._transformWriteCallbackTarget which must implement Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsCallbacks.ITransformWriteCallback will be have Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsCallbacks.ITransformWriteCallback.OnTransformTweenWrite called allowing custom transform tween writing.
Transform tweens are not calculated or written.
Transform tweens are calculated and written in parallel using a Jobs.TransformAccess.

Transform tweens are calculated and written linearly on a single thread, likely the main-thread. This may be faster than using Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.TransformTweenMode.Parallel if the majority of the Transform are not split across hierarchies so that they can be written in parallel. To further clarify, if most of the Transform are not interleaved across different hierarchies, this non-parallel (sequential) mode may be faster than Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.TransformTweenMode.Parallel, because it avoids the overhead of splitting and synchronizing work across multiple threads when there is not enough independent hierarchy work to parallelize efficiently.
Defines how the 2D Transforms from each Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody are written to the 3D Transform system.

Transforms are not written. Instead, the callback target set with Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._transformWriteCallbackTarget which must implement Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsCallbacks.ITransformWriteCallback will have Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsCallbacks.ITransformWriteCallback.OnTransformWrite called allowing custom transform writing.

Transforms are written but the rotation is converted to a Quaternion where only a single axis is written, all others will be set to zero rotation. This is the fastest method of writing transforms however, any 3D rotations or rotations on the unused axis will be reset to zero. The rotational axis written to depends on the current Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.TransformPlane selected with Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._transformPlane where it will always be perpendicular to the transform plane.
Transforms are never written. This is the fastest operation.

Transforms are written but the rotation is converted to a Quaternion where the rotation of the body transform is merged into the existing 3D rotation. This is the slowest method of writing transforms however, all 3D rotations are preserved. The rotational axis written to depends on the current Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.TransformPlane selected with Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._transformPlane where it will always be perpendicular to the transform plane.

summary.para: A Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld definition used to specify important initial properties.
Controls if body update callback targets are automatically called. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.SendBodyUpdateCallbacks.
Controls if shape contact callback targets are automatically called. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.SendContactCallbacks.
Controls if joint threshold callback targets are automatically called. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.SendJointThresholdCallbacks.
Controls if shape trigger callback targets are automatically called. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.SendTriggerCallbacks.

Adjust the bounce threshold, usually in meters per second. It is recommended not to make this value very small because it will prevent bodies from sleeping. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._bounceThreshold.

The expected world capacities used to presize internal allocations when the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld is created. All counts default to zero, in which case the engine uses its own minimum defaults. Presizing avoids reallocations during the first simulation steps for worlds with a known object count. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._capacity.
The contact bounciness with 1 being critical damping (non-dimensional). See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._contactDamping.

Controls if contact filter callbacks will be called. A contact filter callback allows direct control over whether a contact will be created between a pair of shapes. This applies to both triggers and non-triggers but only with Dynamic bodies. These are relatively expensive so disabling them can provide a significant performance benefit. A contact filter callback will call the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape._callbackTarget for both shapes involved if they implement Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsCallbacks.IContactFilterCallback.
The contact stiffness, in cycles per second. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._contactFrequency.

The contact hit event threshold controls the collision speed needed to generate a contact hit event, usually in meters per second. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsEvents.ContactHitEvent. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._contactHitEventThreshold.

The contact recycle distance, in meters. Setting this to zero disables contact point recycling. Contact recycling reuses contact points across simulation time-steps when the relative movement is small. This feature improves stability and performance by around 25% (approximately). Contact points are not recalculated until shapes move more than 5cm (default) relative to each other. Contact recycling skips some updates such as friction, pre-solve (etc) until the contacts are no longer recycled. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._contactRecycleDistance.
The contact speed used to solve overlaps, in meters per second. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._contactSpeed.

Controls if continuous collision detection will be used between Dynamic and Static bodies. Generally you should keep continuous collision enabled to prevent fast moving objects from going through Static objects. The performance gain from disabling continuous collision is minor. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._continuousAllowed
Get a default Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld definition.
Controls what colors are used to draw Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody, Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape, Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsJoint etc. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.DrawColors.
Controls how contact points are drawn. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.DrawContactType.

Controls the draw fill alpha. This is used to scale the interior fill alpha and is only used when Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.DrawFillOptions.Outline is used so that the interior color can be distinguished from the outline color by transparency. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._drawFillAlpha.
Controls how shape geometry is filled when drawing. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.DrawFillOptions.

Limits what gets drawn to a narrow selection. This only affects Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.DrawOptions that are drawing all bodies, shapes etc. It does not affect selected elements or custom drawing. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.IgnoreFilter.
Controls the joint contact force scale used when drawing contact forces. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._drawForceScale.
Controls the joint contact normal scale used when drawing contact normals. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._drawNormalScale.
Limits what gets drawn to a broad selection. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.DrawOptions.
Controls the draw point scale used when drawing points. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._drawPointScale.
Controls the draw thickness (outline and orientation). See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._drawThickness.
GetSet the gravity vector applied to all bodies in the world, usually in ms^2. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._gravity.
Get/Set the maximum linear speed. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._maximumLinearSpeed.

Controls if pre-solve callbacks will be called. This only applies to Dynamic bodies and is ignored for triggers. These are relatively expensive so disabling them can provide a significant performance benefit. A pre-solve callback will call the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsShape._callbackTarget for both shapes involved if they implement Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsCallbacks.IPreSolveCallback.
Get/Set the simulation sub-steps to use during simulation. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.Simulate. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._simulationSubSteps.
Get/Set the simulation mode which controls when or if the simulation will be automatically simulated. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.SimulationType and Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.Simulate.

Get/Set the simulation worker count for the world. A single simulation worker is always used for simulation therefore a worker count of one means single thread simulation only. The actual quantity of workers used will always be capped to those available on the current device and reading the property will return the number of workers actually being used by the device. Changing the worker count continuously is not recommend and will impact performance as it requires the task queue be recreated. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._simulationWorkers.

Controls if bodies go to sleep when not moving and not interacting. Sleeping can provide a significant performance improvement when many Dynamic or Kinematic bodies are in the world. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._sleepingAllowed

Controls if an extra write pass prior to the script fixed-update callback is made for any interpolation tweens to ensure that transforms are synchronized to the final body pose. Because this is an extra write pass, it has an impact on overall performance so only enable if you require transforms synchronized this way.
NOTE: This only affects Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody that have their Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody._transformWriteMode set to Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody.TransformWriteMode.Interpolate.
Controls the transform plane that the world uses when writing transforms. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._transformWriteMode. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._transformPlane.

Controls the transformation for the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.TransformPlane.Custom to allow transformation writing and reading to/from a custom space. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.TransformPlaneCustom.

Controls if and how Transform tweens are calculated and/or written. Transform tweening is where bodies that have their Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody._transformObject set, write to the Transform each frame depending on the specific body Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody.TransformWriteMode set. Regardless of this setting, Transform tweening is never used if the Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._simulationType is Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.SimulationType.Update or Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld._transformWriteMode is Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.TransformWriteMode.Off.

Controls how transform writing is handled. Only bodies that have their Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsBody._transformWriteMode active and produce a Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsEvents.BodyUpdateEvent will write to a transform. See Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsWorld.TransformWriteMode.

member.name: M:Unity.U2D.Physics.PolygonGeometry.CreatePolygons(System.ReadOnlySpan`1<UnityEngine.Vector2>,Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsTransform,Unity.Collections.Allocator)

summary.para: Create multiple Unity.U2D.Physics.PolygonGeometry from a set of vertices. The vertices are assumed to produce a closed loop but can describe a concave shape if required. There must be at least 3 vertices. A limit is imposed on small vertex distances so be aware that this overload uses a vertex scale of Vector2._one so consider using the overload which allows you to increase this if required.

member.param: The vertices to create the polygons from.
The transform used to specify where the geometry is positioned.
The memory allocator to use for the results. This can only be Allocator.Temp, Allocator.TempJob or Allocator.Persistent.

returns.para: The created polygon geometry. This NativeArray must be disposed of after use otherwise leaks will occur. The exception to this is if the array is empty.

member.name: M:Unity.U2D.Physics.PolygonGeometry.CreatePolygons(System.ReadOnlySpan`1<UnityEngine.Vector2>,Unity.U2D.Physics.PhysicsTransform,UnityEngine.Vector2,Unity.Collections.Allocator)

summary.para: Create multiple Unity.U2D.Physics.PolygonGeometry from a set of vertices. The vertices are assumed to produce a closed loop but can describe a concave shape if required. There must be at least 3 vertices. A limit is imposed on small vertex distances so it is recommended that scaling is applied here rather than on the returned geometry so geometry is not discarded due to it being invalid.

member.param: The vertices to create the polygons from.
The transform used to specify where the geometry is positioned.
The scaling to be applied to the vertices.
The memory allocator to use for the results. This can only be Allocator.Temp, Allocator.TempJob or Allocator.Persistent.

returns.para: The created polygon geometry. This NativeArray must be disposed of after use otherwise leaks will occur. The exception to this is if the array is empty.
